brief_premise_refuted.premise_as_given: "`liftPart` and `bathroomPod` ... are documented compound MEMBERS and carry NO defineElement / L0 schema at all -- unlike their parent families."
brief_premise_refuted.verdict: REFUTED IN ITS LOAD-BEARING HALF for bathroomPod. The pod IS NOT A MEMBER -- IT IS A COMPOUND PARENT, and it owns two verbs.
measurements: It owns verbs: PluginRegistry.ts:879 -- 'The bathroom pod owns TWO (`bathroomPod.create` / `bathroomPod.delete`, C109 R-1)'. Probe Q-B lists both on the plumbing descriptor's registered handler types. Probe Q-C dispatched both through the real runtime: they reached canExecute ('podId must be a non-empty string') rather than 'no handler registered' -- which is the difference between an unregistered verb and a registered one given a bad payload.

It is a PARENT, not a member: Id.ts:113-117 -- 'the LOD-300 parametric BATHROOM POD compound parent. A pod OWNS its members -- the WC, the basin, the shower ... through `members[]` + `parentId`, the same ownership mechanism `pool` (ADR-0124 §3), `balcony` and `lift` (C104 §4) use. Every member is a record in the `plumbing` family; the pod mints exactly ONE new family -- itself (C109 §2).'
brief_premise_refuted.the_half_that_holds: 'No defineElement / L0 Zod schema' is TRUE -- confirmed by `grep -rn "defineElement('" packages/schemas/src/` (26 kinds, no bathroomPod) and `grep -rn 'BathroomPodSchema' packages plugins` (the Zod shape is in geometry-plumbing; plugins/plumbing/src/errors.ts:43 has only a BathroomPodSchemaError). But it is deliberate and reasoned at Id.ts:118-127, not an oversight -- and the L0 BRAND is present, so 'no L0 surface' would be wrong.
brief_premise_refuted.why_this_matters: Grouping the pod with liftPart as 'a member with no verb' inverts its actual risk. liftPart genuinely cannot be authored alone. The pod CAN be authored -- from a real plan overlay, today -- and what it cannot do is SURVIVE A RELOAD. Those need opposite responses.

smuggling_question.question: Brief s4 -- 'MEMBER WITH NO CHANNEL, SMUGGLED onto another family's channel' -- one element id appearing on two families?
smuggling_question.verdict: THE POD HAS NO BUS CHANNEL AT ALL -- and that is the honest state, NAMED here. Its members are NOT smuggled: they are `plumbing`-family records BY CONTRACT, each id belonging to exactly one family.
no_channel_measurement: `grep -n 'bathroomPod' packages/runtime-composer/src/CommandEventBridge.ts` -> ZERO hits. There is no `case 'bathroomPod.create':` and no emit.
`grep -rn 'bathroomPod' packages/runtime-composer/src/types.ts` -> 3 hits, all at :2943-2960 describing the store handle; NO `'bathroomPod.created'` event key in the RuntimeEvents map.
So `bathroomPod.create` dispatches, mutates its store, and emits NOTHING on the bus. Unlike water (parent's channel) and liftPart (parent's payload field), the pod has neither.
smuggling_question.how_it_reaches_the_screen_instead: A STORE SUBSCRIPTION, not an event. apps/editor/src/engine/bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts projects pod members into the LEGACY fixture store (`window.plumbingStore`, @pryzm/geometry-plumbing). Attached at boot by initTools §BATH102 (initTools.ts:1739-1768), which warns loudly if `runtime.stores.bathroomPod` is unreadable ('no mesh, no plan symbol, no elevation symbol, no IFC') rather than failing silently.
why_that_is_NOT_smuggling: Each id belongs to ONE family. `fixtureRecordFor` (bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts:153-172) writes `id: m.id` -- the MEMBER's own id -- with `type: 'plumbing_fixture'` and `parentId: pod.id`. The pod's id is never written as a fixture; a member's id is never written as a pod. C109 §2: 'the pod mints exactly ONE new family -- itself'.

The ownership link is EXPLICIT, not spatial: :167-170 -- 'C109 §2.3 -- the OWNERSHIP LINK, on every member. `parentId` is what makes the drill-in, the inspector and the delete-reap answerable from the record rather than from a spatial query (C109 §7 / R-4).'

The members are a PROJECTION, not independent state: the module header states 'They are re-derived from the pod record on every diff and reaped when it leaves', so there is no second authority to drift. C84 EI-1 holds by construction.

⚠ THE ONE REAL CAVEAT, and the module names it itself: 'A member an architect MOVES with `plumbing.move` writes the legacy store directly. Today nothing re-projects an existing pod (there is no `bathroomPod.update` verb -- C109 R-1), so that move survives. ⛔ WHEN AN UPDATE VERB IS MINTED, this is the clause to revisit: a blind re-projection would silently discard the architect's move. **L-11485, OPEN.**'
smuggling_question.closest_of_the_three_to_the_pattern: Yes -- the pod is the only one of the three whose members land in ANOTHER family's store. But it clears the C84 EI-9 test (one id, one family) and its reason is contracted at C109 §2, so calling it smuggling would be wrong. The defect is elsewhere: PERSISTENCE.

findings.claim: The snapshotFamilyCoverage row for bathroomPod is STALE ON THREE COUNTS, and the gate PRINTS IT VERBATIM while exiting 0. The row reads: 'Lane BATH102 has plugins/plumbing/src/bathroomPodStore.ts on disk but UNTRACKED, and it is registered in NEITHER ALL_PLUGINS nor runtime.stores, so no user can author a pod yet and nothing is being destroyed TODAY.' Measured: (1) the file IS git-tracked -- `git ls-files plugins/plumbing/src/bathroomPodStore.ts` returns the path, RC=0; (2) it IS in ALL_PLUGINS (PluginRegistry.ts:619-624) and IS on runtime.stores (probe Q-A, ctor BathroomPodStore); (3) a user CAN author a pod -- BathroomPodPlanToolHandler.ts:330 dispatches from a real plan overlay, pinned by bathroomPodPointerReach.spec.ts:231. So pods ARE being destroyed on reload today. The row's own same-commit rule -- 'When BATH102 registers the storeKey, this row must move to persisted with a bathroomPods key IN THE SAME COMMIT' -- was violated: BATH102 registered the storeKey and the row did not move. The classification (UNPERSISTED) is right; the STATED RATIONALE INVERTS THE SEVERITY, telling a reader this is a pre-emptive placeholder when it is live data loss.

findings.claim: check-snapshot-family-coverage.ts verifies SET EQUALITY between store keys and declared rows, and verifies 26 persistence claims against the snapshot's own fields and writers -- but the row's `reason` string is free prose it never checks. That is how a green gate carried three false statements about the family it was describing. The gate is not wrong about WHAT is unpersisted; it cannot be wrong about that. It has no arm over WHY.

The B7 brief groups bathroomPod with liftPart as a 'documented compound MEMBER' owning no verb. The pod is a compound PARENT (Id.ts:113-117) and owns TWO verbs (PluginRegistry.ts:879, probe Q-B, probe Q-C reaching canExecute rather than 'no handler registered'). Only the 'no L0 Zod schema' half survives, and that half is deliberate and reasoned at Id.ts:118-127. The mis-grouping inverts the fix: liftPart's honest state is 'cannot be authored alone'; the pod's is 'can be authored, cannot survive a reload'.

bathroomPod has NO bus channel whatsoever -- no CommandEventBridge case (grep returns zero) and no RuntimeEvents key. Its render path is a store subscription (subscribeDirty), which the module argues is STRONGER than an event channel because create/undo/redo/delete all arrive through one road with no second channel to drift. Named here rather than smuggled: this is the honest state, it is contracted at C109 §2, and it clears C84 EI-9 (one id, one family).

Pre-logged by the module itself (L-11485, OPEN): when a `bathroomPod.update` verb is minted, a blind re-projection would silently discard an architect's `plumbing.move` on a pod member. Recorded so the update verb is not added without revisiting the clause.
